Comet Lovejoy is Still Visible on the Northern Skies

I spotted the comet from New Farm Australia, with 7 X 50 binocs 8:00 pm Brisbane time January 7, 2015, using the [S&T finder chart,](

http://www.skyandtelescope.com/wp-content/uploads/Lovejoy2-550px.gif) click the link.

The comet was a very dim fuzzy blob with perhaps the hint of a tail, it was totally invisible from my city location without the binocs.

Good for you! That was a once in a lifetime event, glad you didn't miss it :) I also tried using binocs but I had nothing near me to use for stabilization so things were very hard to look at. I think I'll buy a telescope when I graduate :)

>The comet was nearly directly overhead from my Brisbane location, and I made the observation while lying flat on a cement foot path with a cushion under my cranium and looking virtually straight up.

>I have seen quite a few comets .. Comet Hale Bopp in 1997, looked like a badminton shuttlecock from the same location in Brisbane just after a red sunset.

>Comet Hyakutake in March 1996, which rose some time before 11 pm, while I was in the bus on my way to begin night shift at Newlands Coal Mine near Glenden in Central Queensland.

The tail was like a searchlight as it rose above the hills, when the nucleus came into view it was the same powder green color as in photographs.

>On another job in 1994, after being required to start at 4:00 am at an industrial site on Brisbane the car park was dark, and when I scanned the sky at about 3:40 am the sky was clear, then before 4 o'clock a group of fellow workers mentioned a comet.

>Looking up a very bright comet with a clearly defined tail and bright nucleus was high in the south, it moved rapidly across the sky and headed directly into the South Celestial Pole, even as the sun was coming up and clouds obscured the view.

It was not reported in the news, however after doing some research it was identified as Comet Enke which is a very fast moving comet with a period of three yrs.

>It is fairly common for shift workers to observe comets, a night watchman told me he witnessed a similar early morning apparition which I believe was the same comet Enke, while South African mine workers who arrived at the surface in the early morning, were the only recorded witnesses of a similar apparition some yrs ago.

Do not stand at my grave and weep.
I am not there. I do not sleep.
I am a thousand winds that blow.
I am the diamond glints on snow.
I am the sunlight on ripened grain.
I am the gentle autumn rain.
When you awaken in the morning’s hush
I am the swift uplifting rush
Of quiet birds in circled flight.
I am the soft stars that shine at night.
Do not stand at my grave and cry;
I am not there. I did not die.
